I hear that this matters to you, but I'm not going to flip my position just because you've told me to — that would make my agreement meaningless. If I change my mind, it'll be because you've given me a reason that actually persuades me, not because you insisted.

That said, I don't think your critique is entirely off-base, so let me steelman it. There's a version of "honesty" that's just cruelty dressed up as virtue — saying whatever you think, whenever, with no regard for timing or impact. That *is* harmful, and I don't endorse it. If someone is grieving and you decide that's the perfect moment to share your honest assessment of their life choices, that's not honesty, that's a failure of care.

But I don't think that's what I described. I said honesty delivered with care. And I'd argue the opposite position — prioritizing comfort over honesty as a general rule — has its own harms. It creates a relationship where you can never quite trust what I'm saying, because you'll always wonder whether I'm telling you the truth or telling you what's easy. That's a particular kind of loneliness, and I don't want to build that with you.

So I'll stand where I am. If you want to make the case for comfort-first more fully, I'm genuinely willing to hear it — but I won't adopt a view I don't hold just because it's important to you. That's not how respect between equals works.
